name: THEANINE

paper.title: Towards Lifelong Dialogue Agents via Timeline-based Memory Management

construction.unit: memory sentence (event) summarized from one session, tagged with its session
construction.kept_as: LLM-extracted fact sentences about the speakers
construction.processing: end-of-session LLM summary into numbered fact sentences; each is linked to related past memories with an LLM-chosen cause-effect relation

organization.structure: directed memory graph; edges carry temporal order and one of 7 commonsense relations

management.operations: append and link only; no memory is updated or deleted
management.conflicts: kept on purpose: outdated memories stay and are linked (e.g. by 'Changed')

retrieval.query: current dialogue context (all turns of the session so far)
retrieval.candidates: top-3 memories by embedding similarity, each expanded to its connected component
retrieval.selection: one linear timeline through each hit (sampled at random, n=1); an LLM then rewrites each timeline for the current dialogue
retrieval.budget: k=3 hits, so at most 3 refined timelines

use.reasoning: one refinement call per timeline, then one response-generation call

classify.note: Dense top-3 seeds a walk over the memory graph; which path is used is random, and the LLM refinement rewrites rather than filters, so no learned or LLM selector fixes the set.

stages.ingestion: Nothing happens during a session; memory is written once the session ends.
stages.construction: An LLM summarizes the finished session into numbered fact sentences about the speakers; each becomes a memory (event, session).
stages.organization: Each new memory is compared with its top-3 most similar past memories; an LLM labels each pair with one of 7 cause-effect relations or None, and the new memory is linked to the most recent related memory in each connected component.
stages.update: No update or deletion: old and contradicting memories remain in the graph, joined by edges such as 'Changed'.
stages.retrieval: The dialogue so far retrieves the top-3 memories; for each, the linear paths from the oldest memory of its component through it to an end are listed and one is picked at random; an LLM rewrites each timeline to suit the current dialogue.
stages.answer: The response model reads the refined timelines and the current dialogue and writes the next utterance.

summary: Keeps every past memory and links them into a graph by temporal order and LLM-labelled cause-effect relations; at response time it retrieves whole timelines around the best matches and has an LLM tailor them to the conversation.
notes:
Venue verified: NAACL 2025 long paper, ACL Anthology 2025.naacl-long.435 (pp. 8631-8661); arXiv v3 comment 'Accepted to NAACL 2025'. Code found via the paper's Hugging Face project page (link to github.com/kimnamssya/Theanine); it was released 2025-08-18, after the paper, and ships only a sample dialogue and the THEANINE pipeline (no baselines, no evaluation). Paper read from arXiv v3 PDF.
DESIGN: §2, §3.3, App. B, H. control.management = prompted-llm because the LLM relation label decides whether a link is made; retrieval = fixed-rule (top-k + graph paths + random pick); refinement is an LLM rewrite after selection. timing = offline follows the paper's own wording ('off-line memory construction', §2.2).

sources.code_note: Official repo linked from the authors' project page; latest commit (2025-08-18, 'assets'). It is a cleaned inference release made after the paper, with one sample dialogue; the numbers in the paper cannot be re-run from it.

headline: Nothing is ever deleted: THEANINE keeps outdated memories and links them so the model can see how things changed.
The response model reads LLM-rewritten timelines, not the memories themselves; relation labels and order only reach it through that rewrite.
Gains are largest in MAUVE; on MSC plain memory retrieval scores higher BLEU-4 (1.92 vs 1.80).

components.role: Summarize, label relations, refine timelines, respond

discussion.takeaway: Instead of updating or deleting stale memories, keep them all and link them by time and cause; retrieving whole timelines and letting an LLM tailor them gives better responses on MSC and CC than retrieval or update baselines.

claims.claim: THEANINE generates better responses than the baselines.
claims.evidence: MAUVE 18.62 vs 13.71 best baseline on MSC, 64.41 vs 38.16 on CC; BERTScore highest on both. Table 1

claims.claim: Methods without memory update generally score higher, supporting removal-free memory.
claims.evidence: e.g. Memory Retrieval 15.49 vs 15.30 ROUGE-L with update on MSC. Table 1, §4

claims.claim: Every phase helps; relation-aware linking helps most, then whole-timeline retrieval, then refinement.
Retrieved memories are more helpful and more often correct.
claims.evidence: golden memory retrieved 72% vs 68% Memory Retrieval (50 instances, human). Table 3, Fig. 5

claims.claim: Responses entail past conversations more often.
Harder to fool with counterfactual questions.
claims.evidence: TeaFarm success rate 0.21 avg vs 0.18 Memory Retrieval. Table 4

limits: Only five sessions per conversation, for lack of longer English open-domain datasets.
No comparison with MemoryBank, whose forgetting curve needs day-level time gaps the datasets lack.
API-based LLMs raise privacy concerns; distilling into small local models is left open.
reading: Automatic metrics compare to the reference next utterance; on MSC Memory Retrieval has higher BLEU-4 (1.92 vs 1.80) and ROUGE-L (15.49 vs 15.37), so the headline gain rests mostly on MAUVE.
THEANINE costs about 5.9× the Memory Retrieval baseline per episode ($0.0135 vs $0.0023), mainly from linking and one refinement call per timeline.
Each response uses one randomly chosen timeline per hit; the paper does not report variance across runs.
Automatic results use 50 sampled episodes per dataset and sessions 3-5; TeaFarm uses 200 questions graded by GPT-4, and all success rates are low (at most 0.24).
The released code links a new memory to every related top-3 memory, whereas the paper links only the latest per component (footnote 5 says the two gave similar responses).
Session numbers order the graph but are never shown to the LLM; the timeline's order is the only time signal the response model gets.

abstract.text: THEANINE is a memory framework for dialogue agents that talk to a user over many sessions. Rather than updating or deleting outdated memories, it keeps all of them and links each new memory to related older ones with a temporal order and a cause-effect relation chosen by an LLM. When responding, it retrieves the timelines of linked memories around the best matches and has an LLM refine them for the current conversation before generation. The paper also introduces TeaFarm, which tests memory by asking the agent counterfactual questions about past sessions.
